howDoI.q: How do I put several rooms on one map?
How do I keep the screen on one room?
How do I make a door that lands somewhere else on the map?
How do I link to a room that is not next door?
How do I make a door that goes back?
How do I make every door into a room land on the same cell?

pages.head: Welcome
pages.html:
Welcome

Rooms on One Map is a Starter: a small game that shows a few Game-Maker ideas, with signs in the levels that say what you are looking at. It has two short levels about putting many rooms on one map, and takes a few minutes to finish.

Play it first. Then open it in Game-Maker (Edit a copy on the home page keeps the original safe) and read the pages below, which say where each idea is made.

The keys

Left and Right walk. Space jumps. F2 shows your hit points, lives and score. Walk into a door to go through it.

The one idea

A map is 100 blocks wide and 100 high, and the screen shows only 16 by 10 of them. A scene does not need a map of its own. Several scenes can load the same map file, and each one puts the hero down on a different cell of it. Turn scrolling off, and the screen stays on that cell’s room. Each room is a scene, and a door is a link that lands in another cell.

pages.head: Level 1: Four Rooms
pages.html:
Level 1: Four Rooms

The FOUR ROOMS ONE MAP sign stands in the red room. It is one of four rooms in a block of two by two, and the brick walls of each are its own color: red, blue, green and gold. The THIS DOOR LANDS IN ANOTHER CELL sign points at the red door, which takes you to the blue room.

The blue door lands in the green room, which is across the map, not next door (THIS DOOR SKIPS TO THE OTHER SIDE). The green room has two doors: one goes back to blue and one goes on to gold. Try the back door once, then come back and take the other. Eight coins lie along the way, and the gold room’s door takes you to level 2.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 1 is made

  • One map file. Open one.map in the map editor. It holds all four rooms: each is a 16 by 10 block cell, with a ceiling and side walls in brick of its own color and ground below. They sit in a block of two by two, with walls between them.
  • One scene a room. Open the Scenes tab. The red, blue, green and gold rooms are four scenes, and all four load one.map in their map slot.
  • The landing cell is the screen. Each scene’s links land on the middle of its room. PLAYGAME opens the screen 8 blocks left and 5 up from the cell the hero lands on, so the cell sets which room you see.
  • No scrolling. Each scene’s scrolling is set to Never scroll in all four directions, so walking never moves the screen onto the next room. The walls keep you in the room, and they are drawn, not invisible.
  • A door is a link. Each door is a block with a link on it: From is the door’s block here, To is a cell of another scene. The blue door’s To is a cell in the green room, in the bottom left corner of the map. Green’s back door is a second link, from green to blue.
  • Fewer files. Four rooms share one block set and one map, so one edit to a wall changes them all.

pages.head: Level 2: One Landing Cell
pages.html:
Level 2: One Landing Cell

Level 2 is a strip of three rooms on a second map: a green room to the west, a red hub, and a blue room to the east. The ALL DOORS IN LAND HERE sign points at the hub’s doorway. Every door into the hub puts you on that same cell, so the hub always looks the same when you come in.

Take the hub’s three coins and go west. The THE VIEW STARTS WHERE YOU LAND sign says why the screen stays on this room, and the BACK IN THE HUB THE COINS ARE BACK sign tells you what to look for: go back, and they are there again. Your score stays. The KEEP PRIZES WHERE YOU GO ONCE sign in the east room says what to do about it, and the exit takes you to the end.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 2 is made

  • Same idea, a strip. Open two.map: three rooms side by side, each 16 blocks wide. The screen never scrolls, so it never leaves the room it started on.
  • Every way in lands on one cell. The hub is entered from the end of level 1, from the west room and from the east room. All three links have the same To: the middle of the hub. In a room that does not scroll, the landing cell sets the view, so link every way in to the same cell and the room never shifts.
  • The map comes back fresh. Taking a coin changes the map in memory, and a scene loads its map again every time it starts. The hub’s coins are back each visit. Your score, hit points and lives are not part of the map, so they stay. Keep prizes where the hero goes only once, or let them come back on purpose.
  • A free checkpoint. Losing a life starts only the current scene again. Splitting a long stage into scenes on one map saves your place at each split.

pages.head: What it cannot do
pages.html:
What it cannot do

These are the engine’s limits, so you can plan around them.

  • No more than 100 by 100 blocks. A map is that big and no bigger, so rooms on one map share that space. A room of 16 by 10 blocks, walls included, leaves room for sixty rooms at most.
  • No room walls from the engine. Nothing stops the hero walking from one room into the next except what you draw. Draw solid walls, and keep the link’s landing cell in the middle of the room it belongs to.
  • The screen is 16 by 10 blocks. A room bigger than that needs scrolling, and then the view can slide past its edge. Keep a room one screen, or turn scrolling on in only some directions.
  • One link, one direction. A link goes from a block to a cell, and nothing makes a way back. A door that goes back is a second link.
  • A room cannot keep what you did. The map loads fresh each visit, so a coin you took, or a door you opened, is back as it was. Only the score, hit points, lives and what you carry stay.
  • A scene links to a block, not a room. There is no “room” in the file. Rooms are cells you draw and landings you choose.

pages.head: Make it yours
pages.html:
Make it yours

Try one change at a time, and play after each:

  • On the Scenes tab, change where the red door lands. Make it a cell in the gold room and see the view change.
  • Change a scene’s landing cell by three blocks to the left. The screen follows it, and the room edge slides off.
  • Set a scene’s right scrolling to Scroll when the character nears the edge and walk toward the wall.
  • Link the hub’s east door to the west room. Rooms do not have to be in a line.
  • Move a coin in the hub, then leave and come back to see it where you put it.

The home page’s Starters tab has more small games like this one.
